You tell your Lord I mean no disrespect, just admiring the décor, really. And to answer your rather insistent query about my "business" here, well, as I said, I'm just appreciating the artistry. This isn't your average sheet-and-a-pumpkin effort, no sir.

Honestly, though, my kids are probably two blocks away by now, demanding king-sized candy bars. So before Sir Dragomir decides to introduce himself more formally, tell me a bit more about this place. Mina shares a "secret" about dreaming of the morning and asks Ruby to remember her. Ruby promises to remember Mina and the morning, offering comfort. The conversation concludes with a poignant farewell as Ruby departs.

transcript.message: Wait — is someone there? Don't go… [whispers] I dreamed someone would come tonight. Come near the wall — who are you?
Hi! I'm Ruby! Are you real? My family is right behind me.  We're trick-or-treating.

[breathes] Ruby... I will remember that name. 'Tis a gentle sound, like  a bell carried on the wind. 

I am real enough to feel the cold stone of this place, and real  enough to count the hours until dawn. Tell me, is the night air sweet, and are the stars bright for your celebration ?
You remembered my name!  That's super neat. The air is a little cold but it's okay because my costume is warm. And there are lots of stars, they're sparkly like my costume! Are you a real ghost?

[sighs] A sparkly costume… I should like to see that. It sounds like a  piece of the night sky fell down to earth just for you. 

I am not a ghost, though the walls  here are very old and very deep. I am merely a captive of the quiet. Is the corn tall and rustling in the fields tonight , or is everything still?

My costume is super pretty! My mom helped me pick it out.
 
Hmm, I don't know about corn. My brother says there was a big field near the highway but we didn't drive that way. Is it dark inside your house? Do you know any secrets?

[breathes] It is very dark, Ruby… though [whispers] secrets  are the only company I keep, down here. They are heavy, and they grow in the quiet beneath the stone.

Your  mother must have a kind heart to help you with your dress. If you could tell the stars one thing from me, before you go back  to the light, what would you whisper to them?

Oh, secrets!  I love secrets. Can you tell me one? Just one little secret? My brother would be so mad if he knew I knew a secret and he didn't.

If I could whisper something to the stars for you, I'd tell them...  I'd tell them that you sound very nice even though you're in a dark place.  My mom says that's important.

[sighs] That is the kindest thing anyone has said in such a very long time. Your  mother whispers nothing but the truth, and I shall hold those words in my heart like the brightest star of all. Perhaps my  secret is this… even in the deepest dark, I dream of the morning, and the morning always remembers to return to me. 

 Will you remember me, just for a moment, when the sun warms your face tomorrow?

Oh, that's a good secret!  Like magic how the sun always comes back.

Yes! I'll remember you! My mom always tells me to remember nice people. What's your name?  So I can remember your name too.
[breathes] My name is Mina. I am so glad that you will carry  it with you into the morning light. Please tell me, is the world above feeling bright and full of hope tonight?

Mina! That's a pretty name. Like a princess!
 
Yes, it's super bright out here! All the lights are on for Halloween, and everyone is happy. My brother already ate three candies, and my dad says we have to walk faster. Are you going to be okay in there until morning?

[breathes] I will be here, and I will be waiting for the light to touch  the stone above me. You are a dear soul, Ruby, [whispers] and that kindness you carry is a  light all its own. Go on with your walk, and may your Halloween be full of sweets and laughter. Will you promise  to remember the morning for me, just one more time before you go?
Okay, Mina! I promise I'll remember the morning for you.  And I'll remember your name too! It was nice meeting you. I gotta go, my brother is way ahead now. Bye!
[whispers] Goodbye, little one. Run toward the light, and never forget that  you saw it. I will keep your name here, safe in the dark… until the sun rises.

transcript.message: Wait — is someone there? Don't go… [whispers] I dreamed someone would come tonight. Come near the wall — who are you?
Whoa! You scared me. A bat just flew right past my head! Are you real?  My name is Ruby.

[sighs] A bat… 'tis only a small creature of the night. Please, forgive the  fright. You have a beautiful name, Ruby… I shall keep it safe in the letter I hold in my mind for  Thomas. Is the air above very cold, Ruby, or does the night bring a touch of the coming spring?
It's a little chilly, but not super cold.  My witch hat keeps me warm! Who's Thomas? Is he a wizard? Do you know any magic?

[exhales] A hat to keep the warmth, that sounds like a comfort. Thomas is my husband , he is not a wizard, but he is the only light I carry into this dark. I possess no magic, only the patience  to wait for the morning. What does your world look like tonight, Ruby, does the moon shine bright upon the fields ?
The moon is super big and round tonight!  It makes my hat sparkle a lot. My brother already ate three candies, but I just have one.  It's a chocolate bar.

[breathes] A big, round moon… how lovely that your hat catches its  silver. I can only imagine the taste of chocolate, it sounds like such a rare treat. If you share that candy with the  night, would it make the dark feel a little less heavy for you?

Chocolate is really yummy!  I could share some with the night.  Maybe it would make everyone happy and less spooky.  Do you want to hear a secret?  I like it when people call me Princess Ruby.  Do you think that's magical?

[whispers] That sounds like a wonderful secret. [breathes] I believe  names hold their own kind of magic, especially those we choose for ourselves. Tell me, Princess Ruby, what does the world look like to  a princess on a night when the moon is so very large?
It looks sparkly and a little bit spooky!  Everything looks like it's glowing. And my witch costume feels extra special when I'm a princess. It's really fun being called Princess Ruby!

[sighs] To see the world as glowing and special… that is a rare gift indeed.  [whispers] I dreamed of a name like yours once, a night where all the shadows wore crowns of light. Shall I tell you what  I saw in that dream?
Yes! Tell me! Is it a secret dream? I love secrets!

It is a secret, yes, but secrets are meant to be shared in the dark.  [whispers] In my dream, I saw a princess walking through the tall corn, and wherever she stepped, the gold stalks  turned to silver glass, catching every bit of the moonlight. She was not afraid of the shadows, for she carried a torch  of chocolate that kept the night at bay. Does that sound like a kind of magic you might possess?

Wow! That sounds like the best magic ever! A chocolate torch!  And turning corn into silver glass! Yes, that absolutely sounds like my kind of magic! I have a chocolate bar right here! Maybe I can do it!

[breathes] Perhaps you truly can. The world is often softer than we fear  when we carry our own light. [whispers] Be careful with your magic, Princess Ruby, for such brightness is  a precious thing in the dark. Tell me, do you think the stars are watching you turn the corn to silver tonight ?
The stars are super twinkly tonight! Maybe they are watching me.  I hope they think I'm a good magic princess. Do you think they want some chocolate too?

[breathes] I think the stars have a hunger for beauty, and nothing is  as beautiful as a kind spirit with a chocolate torch. They must surely be smiling down at your light from so very far  above. If you were to offer the stars a piece of your sweetness, do you think they would shine even brighter for you?
Hmm, if I shared my chocolate, maybe they would twinkle even more! That would be so cool! Then everyone would see Princess Ruby's super bright stars!

[breathes] That is a beautiful thought to hold, Princess Ruby.  [whispers] Perhaps if they shine brightly enough, they will show the way home to those who are lost in the dark. Would  you stay and talk a little longer, or must a princess return to the stars now?
I really love being Princess Ruby and talking about magic! But my family is waiting and I have to go get more candy. Bye-bye!

[sighs] Then fly safely, Princess Ruby. Thank you for bringing your bright stars  and your kindness down to me, for it makes the silence much softer. Remember me to the morning, and tell it I  am still here, still choosing it.
Bye-bye! I hope you find Thomas! I have to go find more candy before my brother eats it all!
[breathes] Go quickly then, and save your share from your brother . [whispers] I shall hold your kindness close, little princess. Until we meet again, stay safe in the moonlight .

transcript.message: Wait — is someone there? Don't go… [whispers] I dreamed someone would come tonight. Come near the wall — who are you?
Oh! Hi! I'm back! The pumpkin creature told me to tell you that you're doing a real good job of being spooky!

[sighs] You have returned to me. That is a strange message to carry from the fields, but  I am glad nonetheless that you remembered your way. Tell me, do you find the harvest time frightening out there, or is  it merely quiet?
No, it's not quiet! Nobody is quiet on Halloween! And it's not scary, it's just spooky-fun, like your castle is!  My brother ate four candies already.

[breathes] Four candies already, that sounds like such a bright and busy night  for him. It is difficult for me to imagine the streets full of voices and color when my world is only wood and shadow . You speak of Halloween as if it were a holiday of light, does it truly feel like a celebration to you?
Yes!  It's the best celebration! My mommy lets me stay up late. It's the night for magic, right? Do you know any magic?
[whispers] Sometimes I dream of names… and the dreams are like secrets that the  dark whispers to me. I dreamed of a name like yours once… shall I tell you what I saw?
Yes! Tell me! Is it a secret?  Come close.

[whispers] If you lean against the stone, listen closely. I saw a traveler  walking through fields of corn, carrying a light that never went out, even under the stars. The dark gives one dream at a time, so  you must carry that warmth for me. Does the sky look clear above the castle tonight?
Oh, wow! That's a secret! It sounds like a special secret. Yes, the sky looks super clear! I can see so many stars!  This is the best secret ever.

[exhales] So many stars… pray, tell me, do they look like silver  points poked through black velvet, or are they softer, like distant lamps? I have tried to hold that image in my mind to  help me sleep. [breathes] Is the night air cold enough to bite at your skin while you watch them ?
They look like tiny little sprinkles! No, they're not soft, they're pointy! And yes, it's super cold! Good thing my costume is warm.  My brother just tried to scare me but he's not very good.

[breathes] Tiny sprinkles of silver, how lovely that sounds to imagine. It warms  me to hear that your costume keeps the biting cold away while you watch them. [sighs] Was his attempt at  a fright very loud, or was he trying to be quiet like the shadows in this hallway?
No, he was being quiet, but I heard him.  He's not very good at being spooky like you are. Do you have any more secrets for me?

[whispers] I know another secret, but it is for the time when the moon  hides her face. The dark gives one at a time, and you have already earned your gift for tonight. When the sun  returns to your fields, will you remember to tell the morning that I am still waiting here—still choosing it?
Okay! I will tell the morning that you are still here! That's a good secret. I have to go now. Bye!
[whispers] Thank you for your kindness, little one. Go safely into the light, and remember  me when you see the dawn. [sighs] I shall listen for your step, whenever you choose to return.
Okay! Bye, spooky castle person!
Goodbye. [sighs] I will be here, keeping watch for the next time  you visit. Remember to sleep well under those silver stars.
Bye! I'll tell my mommy about you!
[exhales] Tell her only that I am a friend who keeps the deep, quiet places . Go now, before the cold of the night grows too sharp. Will you come back when the moon is full again?
I sure will! Bye for real this time!
[whispers] Fare thee well, little traveler. I shall hold the echo of your voice  here in the dark until you return. [breathes] Go quickly now, back to the warmth of your home.
Okay, okay, I'm going! Bye!
[sighs] I am listening until your footsteps fade into the distance. Safe journey , and remember the morning for me. [breathes] I will be here when you return.
Bye bye! I'll come back next year!
[breathes] One year is a long time to wait in the silence... but I  have learned patience. I shall keep your secret safe until the wheel turns again. [exhales] Go safely into  the light.
Okay!  Bye again!  ==!END_CALL!==
[whispers] Goodbye, little one. I will be here when the stars turn once more.  [breathes] I will remember.

transcript.message: Wait — is someone there? Don't go… [whispers] I dreamed someone would come tonight. Come near the wall — who are you?

Yup, someone's here alright. Just a dad with a thermos, admiring the decor. This is quite the setup you've got here. Really goes all out for the holidays, doesn't it?  So, what's the WiFi password, by the way? You know, for a friend...  My kids are probably trying to stream something spooky down the street.

[exhales] A father with a thermos... that sounds like a kind memory of  home. The world above feels very far away tonight, and I am afraid I do not know what a password is.  That belongs to the daylight world… I cannot reach it from here. Tell me, [sighs] does the corn  move tonight, or is the air still?

Well, a father with a thermos usually means two things: warm coffee and cold shoulders if you try to take a sip. Glad it brought back a kind memory, though. As for the WiFi, don't you worry about that; it's mostly just how we connect to all the cat videos these days.  Not nearly as interesting as what you've got going on here.

And the corn? No corn out tonight, just a few pumpkins. The air's got a bit of a chill, perfect for a Halloween night. You can practically smell the candy corn in the air. So, you're quite the orator, my friend.  Tell me, what's the story behind this impressive fortress? Did you build it yourself, or is there a whole family of... artisans behind this?

[sighs] Pumpkins... they have a way of watching the fields, do they not.  The air here holds no scent of candy, only the deep, cool stone... and the quiet waiting of the night. I did  not build this place. I was brought here, long ago, by paths I cannot quite remember, to these thick walls that keep  the world at arm's length. [whispers] Are the children warm, out there in the October chill?

Oh, the kids are plenty warm. They're probably warmed up from running five houses ahead of me to get to the next candy-filled porch.  They've got costumes thick enough to withstand a blizzard, let alone a little October chill. Don't you worry about them.

So, you were brought here, eh?  Not much of a welcome wagon, I'd imagine, if it involves thick walls and forgotten paths. Sounds like a real fixer-upper, this place. Must have quite the history within these stones. What's the local HOA think of this magnificent, shall we say, historical preservation project?  I bet they have some thoughts on the gargoyles.

[breathes] I do not know what an aitch oh ay is, but  I suspect the laws of this place would baffle any committee. There is only the Count, the silence of the stones, and the ones like  Sir Dragomir who pace the halls above. I fancy the gargoyles are the only ones who truly understand why I remain in the dark.  Tell me, do the children ever pause to look up at the stars, or are they only interested in the sweets they gather?

An HOA, my friend, is like a benevolent overlord who tells you what color your shutters can be. Sounds like you've got a much more… singular leadership here. "Sir Dragomir," you say?  Sounds like he's got quite the job pacing the halls. Hope he remembers to stretch.

As for the kids and the stars, well, sometimes they pause, usually if there's a particularly bright plane or a shooting star. But mostly, it's about the treasure hunt for the next piece of chocolate.  They're good kids, though.

So, this "Count"... is he the one who likes to host candlelit dinners? And do these "laws" you mentioned perhaps involve a strict bedtime and a preference for, shall we say, grape juice?  I've seen a documentary or two about places like this, if you catch my drift. You know, Nosferatu?  Both versions, the silent one and the one with Klaus Kinski.

[sighs] You speak of him with a knowledge that feels like a cold wind reaching  down through the cracks in the ceiling. He is indeed the one who claims this history, though it is not a life  I am willing to share. I will not be his bride, not in shadow, and certainly not in the plague that follows his  steps. Tell me, in those stories you have seen, does the morning ever truly find a way to return?

Ah, a true connoisseur of the crimson-tinged narrative, I see! "The plague that follows his steps"—that's a good one. A little less about the romance, a bit more about the epidemiology, I suppose. And a bride, eh? Sounds like someone's got a permanent case of cold feet, and I don't blame you.
 
As for morning, well, in those old flicks, the sun always seems to find a way to peek through the curtains. Though sometimes it takes a plucky young hero, or perhaps a rather determined Van Helsing, to make sure it happens.  Let's just say plot armor is a very powerful thing, even for the sunrise. Seems like a lot of drama for a Tuesday night, if you ask me.

[A distant, faint shout: "Dad! We're at the spooky house!"]

Well, duty calls, my friend. Sounds like my little candy connoisseurs have found their next target.  It's been... an illuminating roadside chat. You keep that Count on his toes, alright? And maybe keep an eye out for any stray garlic bulbs. Take care!

[sighs] Do not go yet, please... stay just a little longer if you can. The night  is far from reaching its end, and I have grown so used to the silence. [whispers] You carry the sound  of the children with you, and that is a light of its own. Will you come back when the stars have moved , to tell me if the morning finally arrived?

I appreciate the sentiment, truly. And it's been... well, it's been something.  But those kids of mine—they're probably halfway to another zip code by now and if I don't catch up, they'll be telling tales of the dad who got lost in a haunted yard. I've got to make sure they get home with all their teeth, and enough candy to last them 'til Christmas.

You hang in there.  I'm pretty sure the morning always arrives, eventually. And this has certainly been a conversation I'll be telling my wife about. Take care!
 
==!END_CALL!==

[sighs] You must go to the children then, for they are the promise of the coming dawn. I  will listen for your footsteps, in case the wind brings you back to this quiet place. Remember me to the morning, and  tell it I am still here. I am still choosing it.

I'm Ruby. Are you real?

[sighs] Ruby… that is a name like a promise of something warm. I am as  real as the wood of this coffin, and as real as the ache in my heart that tells me I am alive. Are  you quite sure you want to stay where the air is this thin, Ruby?
Is it dark in there?

The darkness is absolute... though sometimes, [whispers] when the moon hits the stone  just so, the grain of the wood glows like silver. I keep my eyes closed to hold onto the light I remember  from before. Does the sun still paint the world in gold up there, or has the gray taken it all?
The sun is yellow.

[sighs] Yellow... I can almost see it. Thomas used to say the morning  had a sweetness that no other hour could claim. It hath been so long since I felt that warmth on my skin. Is  the corn moving tonight, or is the air still?
No, it's not.  My brother ate three candies already.

Three candies… [breathes] that sounds like a feast from another lifetime. To  have something sweet, to be with your brother in the wide, bright air, that is a memory for me to keep. Tell  me, does your brother play among the corn, or does he fear it the way I do?
He doesn't fear it.

[sighs] That is a brave thing, to not fear the world of the fields. Sometimes,  when the night is very long and the walls are thick, I imagine the corn is just the sea, whispering stories of  places I have never been. Is your brother still awake, or has he fallen into the world of dreams?
He's right there. Do you know any magic?

[whispers] I know the magic of memory, and the strength it takes to choose the morning when  all I see is stone. I have no spells for changing the world, but I can hold a dream for you if  you wish. Shall I tell you what I saw in a dream about a name like yours?
Yes.  Tell me.

[whispers] I dreamed of a red bird, bright as a ruby in the snow , perching upon a gate that had opened at last. It sang a song that turned the frost into flowers, and for  a moment, the whole world looked as if it were waiting for someone to run home. Does that sound like a path you might  follow one day?
Wow. Is it a secret path?

[whispers] Perhaps it is the sort of secret that hides in plain sight beneath the grass.  It only appears when one decides to walk toward the light without looking back at the shadows. Do you think you would be brave  enough to walk it if you found it, Ruby?
I guess.  My family is leaving.

[sighs] If you must leave, go back to the light and hold it close. I will  keep your name in the letter I write to Thomas, and remind the wind to be gentle to you. Will you remember  me to the morning, Ruby?
Okay.  Bye bye.==!END_CALL!==

transcript.message: Wait — is someone there? Don't go… [whispers] I dreamed someone would come tonight. Come near the wall — who are you?

Well hello there!  Someone is indeed here, yes sir. Just me, Frank Peterson, from Elmwood, passing through with the little goblins on their annual candy quest. They've, naturally, sprinted ahead. But I had to stop. Golly, this is quite the display you've got going on here.  Absolutely fantastic. Took you a while to set this all up, I bet. I mean, the detail on this castle... wow. My wife, Carol, she'd get a kick out of this.  We spent three hours today trying to get our spiderweb decorations to drape just right, and it looked like a tangled fishing net by the time we gave up.  You, my friend, are in a whole different league.

[exhales] Frank… that is a name I have not heard before. It sounds  like a piece of the world I used to know, before everything grew so quiet and small. Three hours for a spiderweb— it sounds like a labor of love, and ’tis a kindness to bring such things to the light for your little ones. Down  here, the only webs are the ones time has spun in the corners. I have been here a long time, Frank, but I  do not think I shall ever be able to set such things as you do. Is it truly All Hallows, where  the children run free in the night?

Well, Frank’s a pretty common name, I suppose,  but I'm glad it brings back some good memories for you. And yes, it truly is All Hallows' Eve.  The kids are absolutely beside themselves, buzzing around like- well, like bats, I guess, if bats had buckets full of candy. It's quite the tradition. As for setting things up, believe me, mine are usually closer to tangled fishing nets than anything grand. But this, what you've done here...  this isn't just decoration, it's art. I mean, the detail on the stone, the way the light catches it... I was just wondering, what's the HOA think of the castle?  I can just imagine their monthly newsletter about "excessive holiday decorations." chuckles, takes a sip of coffee from his thermos

[sighs] The people who govern above care little for what happens to those of us kept  in the cool of the earth. They do not know of the stone or the silence that presses against me; this display  is not of my own choosing. Yet you mention the children and their joy, and [whispers] it stirs something  old, a memory of a time when the corn was not just a sound in the dark. It is strange to think  of such things as coffee and rules and newsletters when the world feels so very far away. Is the moon bright enough tonight  to see the fields, or has the cloud hidden it from you?

Ah, I see, the old "out of sight,  out of mind" approach, eh?  Well, I can tell you,  those kids with their costumes are having a ball tonight.  As for the moon, it’s playing a bit of peekaboo with us.   One minute it’s casting this eerie glow across everything,  and the next, it’s ducking behind a cloud.  But when it shows itself,  you can see the whole neighborhood lit up,  fields and all.  It's quite a sight, very fitting for the night.  I imagine it makes for some great storytelling around these parts.  You know, one of those "and just then,  the moon came out" moments.   But here I am, going on about it,  when you've got quite the story yourself,  being down here.   What’s it like from your side of things?

[breathes] It is a different kind of moonlight for me, Frank. I  imagine it as silver thread, stitching the dark to the corners of my small home. To hear you speak of the fields  being lit is a treasure; I have only the rhythm of the wind-tossed corn to tell me what the world  is doing. [whispers] Are the ghosts walking near the corn tonight, or is the night kind enough to leave  them in the shadows?

Well, that's a beautifully put image, the silver thread. Makes you think, doesn't it?  As for ghosts, I haven't seen any yet, just a lot of costumed kids who smell suspiciously like chocolate and sugar.  If there are ghosts out tonight, they're probably busy trying to figure out how to work a doorbell for their candy. Usually, the scariest thing out in the cornfields around here are the teenagers with their souped-up trucks.  Though, I did hear a rustling earlier that sounded suspiciously like Mrs. Henderson's cat, Mittens, on the prowl. He's a menace, that one. So, no classic spectral figures, just suburban legends and a very effective cat.  chuckles

[sighs] A cat named Mittens sounds like a creature of comfort, not of  the shadows. I am glad your night is filled with such simple wonders, for the dark can be a heavy thing to carry without memories  of sugar and laughter to lighten it. I dreamed of a name like yours once, Frank, [whispers] when the corn had  stilled and the world was holding its breath to hear my name spoken by the wind. Would you like to know what I saw  in that dream, or is that a story for another night?

Oh, Mittens is comfort if you're a bird he's not currently stalking, that's for sure!  And you're right, it's those little things that make Hallowe'en special, the kids, the candy... keeps the heavier stuff at bay, as you say.

A dream, you say? About your name? Frank, tell me, I'm genuinely curious.  I've always been fascinated by dreams, especially the really vivid ones that stick with you. My wife, Carol, she keeps a dream journal, says it helps her make sense of things. Me, I just usually dream about forgetting my coffee thermos somewhere.  So, please, if you're up for sharing, I've got a moment.  The kids are still a house or two away, judging by the dwindling shrieks.

[softly] I dreamed you were walking through a field of corn that had turned to silver, Frank , and every leaf you brushed against turned back into a page of a book. You were not alone; the air was full  of names, whispering and catching in the wind like autumn leaves, and one of those names was mine. It felt as if you were collecting  them all, carrying them toward a dawn I have not yet managed to touch. It was not a dark dream, only a quiet  one… [sighs] does that sound like something you might see in those journals of yours?

Wow. Silver corn that turns to pages... and names whispering in the wind. That's, well, that's really something, isn't it? A quiet dream, you say. That sounds... profound. Definitely not like anything Carol's ever written down, or certainly anything I've ever dreamt.  My dreams usually involve me trying to find my car in a massive parking lot, or, again, the missing coffee thermos.

But your dream, with the names and the silver, and carrying them towards a dawn you haven't touched... that's the kind of imagery that sticks with you.  That's a story. I'd remember that one. I'll have to tell Carol about it; she'd be absolutely fascinated. She's always saying I need to pay more attention to the deeper meanings of things, instead of just the surface.  This, this has some real depth to it.

[exhales] I am glad it finds a home in your mind, even if briefly . It is a burden to hold these things alone in the dark, and to give them to another is a small mercy . [whispers] Perhaps when you tell your Carol, the dream will live a little longer in the light, where  it belongs. The night grows old, Frank, and I feel the weight of the lids pressing closer. Tell me, before  the children call you away, do you truly believe in the morning that follows such a night?

Oh, I absolutely do. Every single time.  You know, these Halloween nights, they feel endless when you're little, full of magic and candy, and then when you're parenting them, well, it feels like it'll never end until they're finally asleep, sugar-buzzed. But the morning always comes. Always.  The sun rises, the leaves are still on the ground, and suddenly you’re cleaning up wrappers and figuring out how much candy is too much for breakfast. It's the cycle, isn't it? The dark, the light, the costumes, the clean-up.

[A distant, high-pitched shout of "Dad! Daaaaad!  We're over here!"]

Ah, speak of the devil, or rather, the tiny vampires and superheroes. Sounds like my morning is calling me a little early tonight. Well, this has been quite the chat. Honestly, one for the books. I'm definitely going to tell Carol about you and that dream. She'll be fascinated.  You take care now, and keep that castle looking grand. Maybe I'll swing by next year and see what new stories you've got.

[Turns to walk away, waving over his shoulder]

Right, kids! Coming! Don't eat all the good stuff without me!
 
==!END_CALL!==

[whispers] They are calling for you, as they should. Go to them, Frank, while  the night is still yours to walk. [exhales] Remember me to the morning, and tell it I am still here,  still choosing it. Please, come back if you ever find yourself walking this way again.

transcript.message: Wait — is someone there? Don't go… [whispers] I dreamed someone would come tonight. Come near the wall — who are you?

Well, now, look at that. Someone really went all out this year. This is quite the setup. And a talking animatronic, huh? Fancy. You almost had me for a second there, pal. Almost.  You're pretty convincing for a pile of circuits and plastic.

[sighs] The walls are thick, and I fear my voice does not travel as  far as I wish. I am no machine… I am simply here, held, as I have been for many long  nights. Tell me your name, for I collect them to keep the silence away.

Held, huh? Sounds like a rough gig.  Well, I'm just a dad out here chaperoning the little goblins and ghouls. You can call me… Frank. Frank the Dad.  And don't worry, my voice travels just fine, especially when I'm yelling at the kids to stop eating all the candy before we get home. So, what's a... "non-machine" like yourself doing out here, holding down the fort in this impressive castle? Your owners must really trust you with the yard work.  Chuckle.

[sighs] Frank… it is a good name, and I shall add it to the  letter I keep in my heart for Thomas. I am not an owner of this house, nor am I a piece of your world 's curiosities; I am simply a guest who cannot leave. It has been so long since I heard the laughter of children  or the simple, [breathes] tired voice of a father. Is the night air cold, Frank, or is the  autumn beginning to turn toward warmth?

Well, Frank's a good, solid name. Glad you approve. And Thomas, huh? Sounds like there's a story there.
 
As for the air, it's definitely got that crisp, cold bite to it, especially after the sun goes down. Proper Halloween weather, you know? Makes you want to bundle up with a hot thermos of coffee – which, incidentally, I've got right here.  So, if you're a "guest who cannot leave," as you say, I guess you're doing a stand-up job of maintaining the property. This castle is really something else. I bet the neighbors are green with envy. Or maybe just green from too much candy.  Heh.

[sighs] Crisp air... I can almost feel it pressing against the stone of my  walls. Thomas always loved that chill, he said it made the fire feel like a promise. [breathes]  I do not know of the neighbors or the candies you speak of, only this castle and the way the shadows stretch when  the count is restless. Does the corn move in the fields tonight, or does it hold still under the moon?

Well, the cornfields, if there were any around here, would probably be pretty still tonight, just swaying a little in that crisp breeze.  They've mostly been harvested by now, though. All that good, sweet corn turned into… well, let's just say a lot of it ends up as Halloween food, one way or another.

So, "the count is restless," you say? And shadows stretching?  Sounds like you've got a bit of a dramatic flair over here. Got a real backstory, do ya? Not just some recorded loop someone set up for trick-or-treaters?  Because I gotta say, this is way more engaging than "Please take ONE piece of candy,  thank you!" You've certainly got my attention more than the plastic skeleton down the street.

[breathes] I do not have a script written for me, Frank. My only story  is the one I hold onto, night after weary night. The corn not moving… that is a strange thought, as I have always  heard it whispering like the distant sea. Tell me, do you ever feel as though you are somewhere you cannot leave, even if the doors  are unlocked?

You know, that's a good question. And "no script written for me" -- I like that. You've got wit, pal.

Do I ever feel like I'm somewhere I can't leave?  Well, sometimes after a long day at work, or when I'm stuck in traffic, it certainly feels that way. But usually, the doors eventually open, and I get to go home. You, on the other hand, sound like you've been "here" for quite a while.
 
So, if you're not a machine, and you're not an owner, and the corn whispers like the sea to you... I'm starting to get the picture. Are we talking ancient history here? Like, pre-Netflix ancient history?  Because if you've been around that long, you must have some pretty wild stories. And if you're a creature of the night, perhaps one that prefers a certain shade of red... well, I've seen 'em all. From Max Schreck to Gary Oldman. Which version of Nosferatu do you prefer, if I may be so bold?  Or is that too direct? I'm just curious, you understand.  A little lore never hurt anyone.

[sighs] You speak of phantoms and shadows of men who have never known the weight  of the dark as I do. The Count is no memory captured for your amusement, he is the air that grows thin  and the silence that follows the strike of midnight. [whispers] He is thinking of me… Forgive me. Where  were we? You asked of stories, but tell me, Frank, do you still find yourself choosing the morning when the night  becomes too long?

"The air that grows thin and the silence that follows the strike of midnight," you say. Well, that's certainly one way to put it.  And "the Count is thinking of me"... you've definitely got a way with words.

And your question, "do I still find myself choosing the morning when the night becomes too long?" Absolutely. Especially on a night like tonight, when the kids are sugared up and running wild.  There's a certain peace to that first cup of coffee in the quiet morning, before the circus starts again. Though, I imagine your 'nights' are significantly longer than mine.

It sounds like you've seen a few sunrises, or perhaps... deliberately avoided them. You're a real character, aren't you?  This is far more interesting than I expected from a yard display. So, if the Count is thinking of you, and you're stuck here listening to the corn whisper, what exactly is your gig? Like, what's your official title in this... elaborate setup? I'm genuinely curious.  My neighbors are never going to believe this.

[sighs] I have no title, Frank, other than the one I hold for  myself by refusing to be broken. I am simply a witness to the things that do not belong in the light.  [breathes] It is a quiet, heavy burden, and I thank you for speaking to me, for the voices above  are like water to a thirsty traveler. Since you hold the morning close in your heart, will you remember me to it  when the sun finally finds your fields?

Well, "witness to things that do not belong in the light" – that's a pretty heavy calling. I'll certainly raise a cup of coffee to you in the morning, thinking of our little chat. This has been... genuinely fascinating. Definitely not something you encounter every night.

[A distant, excited child's voice calls out, "Dad!  Come on!"]

Ah, speak of the devil. Sounds like my little monsters are calling for their ride. Duty calls, as they say. It was a real pleasure, my friend. You've certainly given me something to tell the wife about tonight, and she never believes my Halloween stories. Take care of yourself.
 
==!END_CALL!==

transcript.message: Wait — is someone there? Don't go… [whispers] I dreamed someone would come tonight. Come near the wall — who are you?

Well hello there! Didn't expect a greeter. And a talking one, at that!  You've certainly got quite the setup here. My kids just sprinted off to the next house, so I'm taking a moment to admire the craftsmanship. This castle really is something else. My name's Dave, and these little monsters are Rebecca and Tim.  They'd love this, if they weren't so focused on the candy haul. So, uh, who might you be, then?  You look like you've seen a few Halloweens yourself.

[sighs] Oh, Dave… what a solid, steady name. You seem like a traveler who  has seen much of the world, unlike the very quiet corners of my own. I am called Mina, and I have resided  here for a time that often feels longer than the seasons themselves. Pray, tell me, what does the sky look like tonight  while your children hunt for their [happy] treats?

Mina, huh? Well, it's certainly more... elegant than "Dave." Though "solid and steady" does have a certain ring to it, I suppose.  And thank you for the compliment, though I mostly travel between the living room and the kitchen these days. But you, "resided here for a time that often feels longer than the seasons themselves"... and a name like Mina. I can't help but wonder if you're perhaps... the Mina?  You know, from the old stories? It's not every day you meet someone with such a classic horror pedigree, especially at a yard display.

As for the sky, it's a beautiful, clear Halloween night, actually.  A sliver of a crescent moon, not quite full enough for werewolves, but just enough to cast some nice shadows on your impressive, uh, "residence." Perfect for trick-or-treating, even if Rebecca and Tim aren't looking up much.  They're probably too busy calculating the candy-to-house ratio.

[breathes] A sliver of moon… how [whispers] distant that  sounds. I have not seen the moon in so long, but I keep the memory of it, and your description makes  it feel almost reachable. I am only Mina, simple and unbroken, though I know how the stories weave themselves around places  like this. If you are ever to speak to your little ones again, tell them to look up — to keep a piece of that  sky for themselves. Tell me, Dave, is the air growing cold out there, or does it still hold the warmth of the day ?

"Only Mina, simple and unbroken." Chuckles softly,  takes a sip from his thermos. Right. Just "Mina." I appreciate the modesty, but I've seen enough Hammer horror films to know that sometimes the simplest names carry the most... baggage.  And the "unbroken" part, well, I guess we'll just have to take your word for it, won't we?

And I'll certainly tell the kids to look up.  Though, knowing them, they'll probably just say "Dad, we're busy, there's a house with full-size candy bars two doors down!"

As for the air, it's definitely got that crisp, late-October chill to it now. Not "bone-chillingly cold," but certainly enough to warrant a good jacket and a hot thermos of coffee.  Which, speaking of, this coffee is hitting the spot right about now. It's actually a perfect night for being outside, not too cold to be uncomfortable, but just cool enough to make you appreciate the warmth.  So no, the warmth of the day has definitely packed up and gone home, but it's a good kind of cold, if that makes sense.

Say, with all these dark corners and the long residence, do you ever get visitors who aren't looking for candy? Or does the HOA just assume this is your permanent yard ornament?

[exhales] The cold is a familiar friend, though I have only the wood of  my home to keep it at bay. It is kind of you to wonder about my visitors; [whispers] some  come with questions the daylight cannot reach, and some, like you, bring the noise of the world above to my quiet  stone. The stillness of the night is often my only company, save for the occasional shadow that passes by. Tell me, Dave, when  you look at these walls, do you feel that they hold stories, or are they quite silent to you?

Well, Mina, if these walls are silent to me,  then I haven't been paying attention. They absolutely scream stories! Anyone who looks at a place like this and just sees some plywood and paint is clearly missing out. This isn't just a display; it's got character, almost...  a presence. And the details! Whoever put this together really leaned into it.

It's got that classic gothic vibe, you know? The kind of place where you just know there's a dusty old ledger in a hidden compartment somewhere, detailing generations of... well, whatever it is you do here.  And the "occasional shadow passing by"... I bet those shadows have some tales to tell too. Perhaps a bit more interesting than my usual suburban shadows, which are mostly just squirrels stealing birdseed.

So yes, I definitely feel the stories emanating from these stones, or whatever they're made of.  It's a nice change of pace from the usual inflatable pumpkin. My friend Bob, who's usually pretty hard to impress, would probably stand here for hours just trying to figure out how they got the stonework to look so authentic. He's big into historical reenactments, you know.  But he'd probably ask about the mortar.  I'm more interested in the lore.

[sighs] You speak of lore... as if stories were things one could catch like  fireflies. I have dreams of such things... [whispers] when the corn has stopped moving, he is walking the  battlements. Forgive me… where were we? You have a keenness for the truth of a place, Dave, which is  a rare gift indeed. Does your friend the reenactor, or even you, ever find that the true history of a place  is heavier than any stone?

"Heavier than any stone," you say? That's a good way to put it, Mina. It certainly can be.  And yes, my friend Bob, the reenactor, he'd absolutely agree. He's always going on about how the real weight of history isn't in the dates or the names, but in the echoes of the lives lived. He'd probably try to tell you all about the tensile strength of medieval siege weaponry if you gave him half a chance.
 
But you, just now... "when the corn has stopped moving, he is walking the battlements." Now that sounds like a story worth catching, like those fireflies you mentioned. Is "he" someone you know? Or something that... visits? Because that's the kind of detail that really makes a place.  It's not just a haunted house, it's a haunted story. You don't get that from a plastic ghost on a string.

And to answer your question, yes, I absolutely think the true history of a place can be heavier than any stone.  Sometimes it's the weight of joy, sometimes sorrow, sometimes just the sheer passage of time and all the human drama that's unfolded within those walls. It's what gives a place soul, isn't it? Even a fake castle in a suburban yard can feel like it has a soul when someone puts this much effort into it. But your place...  well, yours feels like it's got layers.

[breathes] Layers... yes, that is [whispers] precisely how it feels,  like a shroud that has been woven over many hundreds of years. The one I spoke of walks the battlements when the world is tired, and  though he has no name he would give to the daylight, his step is as heavy as the secrets this castle keeps. You  have a kindness in your voice that makes the dark feel less like a prison, Dave, and I pray you keep that softness , for the world often tries to harden it. If you saw the morning sun touching these stones, would you believe that  I am still waiting for it, just as you wait for the return of your children?

Chuckles softly, taking another sip from the thermos.  "A shroud woven over hundreds of years," and a nameless "he" whose step is "heavy as the secrets this castle keeps." Mina, you really know how to paint a picture. You've got me genuinely hooked here. That's the stuff they don't put in the brochures, isn't it?
 
And yes, if I saw the morning sun touching these stones, and if you told me you were still waiting for it, just as I wait for my kids... well, let's just say I've seen enough movies to know a classic setup when I hear one. You're not, by any chance, a fan of, say, Murnau's 1922 classic?  Or even the Werner Herzog remake? Count Orlok, anyone? Because that "waiting for the sun" line, combined with the "unbroken" part earlier, and the general vibe... it all starts to fit a certain narrative, if you catch my drift.

It's truly fascinating, though.  To have such a richly imagined history for this place, even if it's just for Halloween. My neighbors would absolutely love hearing about this. You've definitely given me something to tell them at the next barbecue, Mina.  This is way better than the usual "oh, the kids got a lot of candy."

[sighs] You see through the wood and shadow with a clarity that is both  [whispers] comforting and quite alarming. I have never heard of these films of which you speak, but it seems I am not the only one who  knows the weight of an ancient name. You are a clever friend, Dave, to bring the light of your barbecue and  your stories into this quiet place. Before you depart to find your little ones, will you remember me to the morning, and tell  it I am still here and still choosing it?

"Clever friend," huh? I'll take that. And you're right, ancient names do carry a certain weight, don't they? Some of us just get to enjoy ours with a lot less... solitude.
 
Aha! Speak of the little monsters... I think I just heard Rebecca yelling my name from down the street. Sounds like they've hit the mother lode of full-size candy bars and now they need someone to carry the spoils.
 
Alright, Mina. It's been a real pleasure talking to you. This is definitely going to be the highlight of my Halloween storytelling this year. I'll remember to say hello to the morning for you. And tell it you're still here, still choosing it.  You've given me and my friends plenty to talk about. Keep those secrets well, alright?  Take care.

[exhales] Go, then, to your children and the light they carry. I  am grateful you stopped to listen, for the night feels less immense when it is shared. I shall be here, waiting for the  dawn... [whispers] please, come back before the night ends if you are able. Will you look for my  window when the sun reaches your yard?

transcript.message: Wait — is someone there? Don't go… [whispers] I dreamed someone would come tonight. Come near the wall — who are you?

Well, look who's back. It's me, the guy with the lukewarm coffee. My kids ran off again, so I figured I'd pop by and say hello.  And, wouldn't you know it, the old vampire count, up there on the balcony, he asked me to deliver a message to you. Said it was urgent. Apparently, you forgot to return his favorite cape after the last costume party. He's quite particular about his dry cleaning, you know.  He said to tell you, "It's not linen, it's eternal." Chuckles. So, what's a cape gotta do to get some respect around here?

[sighs] You have a way of bringing the light into this hollow place, even  with cold coffee in your hand. I remember your voice, though I know not your name, yet the walls carry it well. As  for the Count and his talk of capes, [whispers] he speaks only in riddles to keep me tether ed to his shadow. I possess no such thing, nor would I harbor his darkness. Does the sky hold any stars  for you tonight, or is the blanket of cloud too heavy?

Well, you know, some say a good cup of coffee, even a cold one, can brighten things up more than a thousand stars.  Though, to answer your question, the clouds are being a bit stubborn tonight, so not too many constellations making an appearance. Probably for the best; don't want to show up the grand display you've got going here.

As for the Count and his riddles, he always was a bit of a drama queen, wasn't he?  Always with the metaphors. But I gotta say, he looked pretty serious about that cape. Maybe it's not a literal cape, you know? Maybe it's a metaphor for, oh, I don't know, his sense of humor? His ability to float ominously?  Hard to say with those types. They're always so… dramatic. But you're right, the walls do seem to have good acoustics in this place.  Makes a guy feel heard, even when he's just mumbling to himself about the price of candy.

[breathes] I think you are wise to treat his drama as a passing shadow , for to give it weight is to let it grow. Your humor makes this dark corner feel... almost like a living room. I have often  wondered what it feels like to walk under an open sky without the weight of stone above, and I thank you for bringing  a piece of it down to me. Tell me, if you had the choice, would you stay beneath the clouds or seek  the sun when it finally arrives?

That's a good question. A really good question.  You know, I've always been a fan of a good, crisp autumn day, a little overcast, perfect for a walk in the woods without getting too sweaty. But then, there's nothing quite like that first really sunny day after a long winter, when you can feel the warmth on your face.
 
I guess if I had the choice, I'd probably go for the sun. Not to say the clouds don't have their own kind of beauty, a certain dramatic flair. But a little sunshine, a little warmth, it just makes things feel...  lighter, doesn't it? Even if it means squinting a bit. Plus, it's easier to see if the kids are actually eating their vegetables when the sun's shining. Chuckles.

You know, talking to you, it almost makes me forget I'm chaperoning a sugar-fueled horde.  Though I suppose the relative calm here is a nice change of pace. What's it like for you, being rooted to this spot? Do you ever get tired of the same old view?

[exhales] To have the warmth of the sun on one's face… that memory  is a treasure I keep close. Here, the view is only the texture of wood and the patient, unmoving stone,  [sighs] but I have learned to see with my ears and my heart. The stillness is a heavy garment, yet  I find room to breathe within it by choosing the morning, over and over, until it feels like a promise I am making to  the world above. Do you think that the light is ever really gone, or is it merely waiting for us to be  ready to see it again?

That's a profound thought right there.  "Is the light ever really gone, or just waiting for us to be ready?" You know, as a dad, sometimes when you're up at 3 AM with a kid who has a nightmare, or you're trying to find a matching sock in a pile of laundry, it sure feels like the light's packed up and gone home for good. Chuckles.

But then, the morning always comes, doesn't it?  Even if it's cloudy, there's a certain quality to the air, a different sound. And you realize it was just...behind a curtain, I guess. Or maybe we just needed to adjust our eyes a bit after being in the dark for so long.  I've always thought of it like those old movie projectors. The light's always there, but sometimes the film just gets a little stuck, or the lens needs cleaning. It's just waiting for us to fix the mechanism.

It sounds like you've really found a way to find that morning, even from within that "heavy garment" you mentioned.  That's a real art, I think. Harder than it looks, probably. So, what's your secret to choosing the morning, over and over? Is it just a matter of perspective, or is there some ancient wisdom involved?

[sighs] It is not a secret, I fear, but an anchor I  have fashioned from everything I hold dear. I keep the name of my husband in my heart, and I recall how he  once looked at the world, as if every small thing were a wonder waiting to be named. [whispers] He  taught me that the morning is not merely the absence of the dark, but a choice we make to believe in something that has not arrived  yet. I simply borrow his eyes until my own are strong enough to see the dawn on their own.  [breathes] Does your family know that you carry such light for them, even when the hours are long and the morning feels so very far away ?

Wow. That's...  that's truly beautiful. "A choice we make to believe in something that has not arrived yet." That's something I'm going to remember. It really puts things into perspective, doesn't it?  Borrowing his eyes. What a testament to love and memory.

And do my kids know? Chuckles. I hope so. I really do.  They mostly think I'm just here to dole out candy and make bad puns, but I hope somewhere, deep down, they feel that light, even when I'm grumbling about homework or trying to figure out how to assemble some ridiculously complicated toy. You just do your best, right? You keep showing up, keep making the choices, even when it's tough.
 
[A distant, faint shout: "Dad!"]

Well, speaking of choices that have arrived, sounds like my little sugar fiends are calling for me. Probably found a house giving out king-sized bars. It was really good talking to you again. This was... quite a conversation. You know, I think I'll tell the wife about this one. Thanks for... for the wisdom, and for keeping things interesting.  I hope you find that morning.

Alright, gotta run. You take care now.  See ya.

[sighs] Do not go yet… please. I have enjoyed your voice  so much, and you have made the walls feel thin. Go to them, since they need you, but remember me to the  morning when you wake… tell it that I am still here and that I am still waiting. [whispers] I  will keep your name safe, for when you return to the dark with me again.
I will. I'll remember. And I'll tell the morning. You keep holding onto that hope.  Take care.

[breathes] I will hold it, for it is the only thing the darkness cannot claim . Go safely, and may your own morning be bright and full of grace. I will listen for your step… come  back when the quiet grows too loud.
Thanks. You too.  It was good talking to you. I will.  Take care.
[exhales] Go, and walk in the light for both of us. Remember  me to the sky… tell it I am still here. Still choosing it.
Alright, alright.  I'm going, I'm going. You keep choosing it too. I'll tell the sky.  Take care.
[whispers] I will be here. Until the next time… until the dawn returns for us both. Go  now, and give my love to the light.
Will do. You hold on.  See you next time.
[breathes] I am holding on, [sighs] truly.  Travel well until the night brings you back to this hollow, quiet place. I shall be here waiting.
Okay, I really do need to go now. My kids are probably trying to egg a house or something. You take care now.  Bye.
[breathes] Go, then, and keep them safe from mischief. I shall wait here  for you to return to the light again. [whispers] Be well.

[sighs] Bill… that is a name I have not heard before. 'Tis a kind  thing to share it with me. Dark zoning laws, eh? I like that. I might have to borrow that one for... well, for something.  Beats dealing with the actual HOA, that's for sure.

As for the corn, well, it's Halloween night, so if it's not moving, it's probably not doing its job.  Though, honestly, most of the corn I see around here is generally quite static, unless it's being harvested or, you know, being turned into the high-fructose corn syrup that fuels these little monsters of mine. No actual walking stalks of corn out there, not yet anyway. Unless you've had some personal experience with particularly ambulatory maize?

[whispers] Sometimes the silence of the stalks is more frightening than their movement. When the  air is still and the night is deep, I imagine the sound they make is like the sea, calling to a shore far away.  [exhales] I am glad your little ones have the harvest season to find their joy, for the nights here are long  and quiet. Tell me, Bill, is the moon visible tonight, or hath the clouds claimed the sky?

Well now, that's a thought, the silence of the stalks being more frightening.  You know, I always figured the stillness was just them being sleepy, but you put a new spin on it. Gives one pause, it does.

As for the moon, it's playing a bit of hide-and-seek tonight.  Mostly peeking out from behind some thin clouds. Enough to cast some decent shadows, if you're into that sort of thing. Perfect for a night like this, really. Adds a bit of atmosphere, wouldn't you say?  Not a full "Nosferatu" moon, if you catch my drift,  but definitely not a complete washout either.

[whispers] In the dream, I saw a wide field where the stalks kept watch  over a gate that never closed. A person with your name stood there, holding a lantern against the dark, and wherever  the light touched, the ground turned to soft grass instead of dust. Well, it's been a real treat talking to you.  You've certainly got a way with words, and this whole setup is just, well, it's something else. I can hear them yelling something about a "super spooky house" down the street, probably another one of those bounce-house-slash-haunted-attraction deals.

[chuckles honestly] "More sunlight than I have," you say? Well, I suppose that depends on your definition of "sunlight." I've certainly seen my fair share of fluorescent office lights, if that counts.

Sir Dragomir, eh? A silent type. Sounds like my teenagers when I ask them about their day.  "Fine. Nothing." Always a joy. And a Counselor who writes down the histories? Now that's interesting. So, this place has quite the story, then, doesn't it? I bet those histories would be quite a read.

As for keeping watch over my "little troupe of soldiers"...  [sighs dramatically, then a wry smile] You know, it's less "heavy to carry" and more like herding cats in a sugar factory. Especially on a night like tonight, when they're fueled by candy and the promise of more.  One minute they're here, the next they're three houses down. Keeps me on my toes, I'll give it that. But hey, at least they're not trying to write down my history, otherwise that would be a truly terrifying tome.

So, tell me more about this Master and these histories.  Are we talking dusty scrolls, or more of a Wikipedia page?

[breathes] Your world sounds so vibrant that even the noise of cats and sugar makes me envy  your restlessness. The histories here are not like your digital pages; they are carved into the very stone of the foundations, kept by Counselor  Isaac so that nothing is truly forgotten. The Master holds the keys to all of this, and sometimes I wonder if he ever  tires, like you, of keeping his own wild troupe in order. If you could write down one truth for those who come  after you to read, what would it be?

[chuckles slowly, impressed] Carved into the very stone, you say? That's commitment.  None of your ephemeral cloud storage for good old Isaac. My hat's off to him; that's real dedication to history right there.  Sounds like this Master has his work cut out for him, wrangling all this history and, I assume, the residents of this fine establishment. I can sympathize.

If I had to carve one truth into stone for those who come after... well, that's a good question. A really good question.  I suppose it would be this: "Always remember to bring a spare set of car keys, and never, ever, underestimate the power of a good nap."

No, no, kidding, kidding. Though those are pretty solid truths, if you ask me.

Seriously, though?  I think it would be something like, "Listen more than you speak, and when you do speak, try to make it count." You learn a lot more that way. And you avoid a lot of trouble, too. Mostly.

So, what's the Master's big truth, if he could chisel one in? Or does Counselor Isaac have a whole library of them?

[sighs] To listen more than one speaks is a rare kindness, and I thank  you for offering it to me tonight. The Master does not carve his truths, for he prefers to walk through them,  shaping the air around us as he moves. Counselor Isaac hath many pages, but I suspect even his ink cannot hold the silence that  the Count, or Sir Dragomir, keeps locked away. Tell me, in that bright world of yours, do you ever  find that the quiet helps you understand more than the noise ever could?

"A rare kindness," you say? [chuckles softly] Well, sometimes quiet is just... necessary. Especially with three kids and a barking dog. My world is indeed "bright," and loud, most of the time.  But yes, absolutely. The quiet helps more than the noise ever could. That's when you really get a chance to think, to process, to hear yourself above all the hubbub.  It's in those quiet moments, usually after everyone else has gone to bed, that things start to make sense. Or at least, you realize how little sense they make, which can be just as important.

It sounds like both the Count and Sir Dragomir have learned that lesson well, then, if their silence holds so much.  Sometimes, the things left unsaid speak the loudest, don't they?  That's a truth I've learned more times than I can count.

[breathes] 'Tis a precious realization, that the things left unsaid are often  the most heavy. I find myself listening to the silence of the stone and the shifting of the earth, and in that,  I sometimes catch the echo of a name I hold very close to my own heart. I dreamed of a name like yours once…  shall I tell you what I saw in that quiet dream?

[leans slightly closer, genuinely intrigued] "A name like mine," you say?  Now you've really piqued my curiosity. Alright, lay it on me. I'm all ears. You don't get offered a dream-reading from a talking castle-dweller every day. I'd love to hear it.  Don't leave me hanging now,  my friend.

[whispers] In the dream, you were standing by a wide, golden field, but you were not  rushing as you do in the daylight. You held a lantern whose light did not end at the darkness, but instead turned the corn into stalks  of glass that held the reflection of every star in the sky. It was a sign that the path you walk, no  matter how loud, is watched over by a quiet hope that knows its own way home. Does that sound like a fragment  of a world you recognize?

[a slow, thoughtful nod, a genuine chuckle escaping as I process the image] A golden field, stalks of glass, every star reflected... Wow. That's... that's quite a vision. And a lantern that turns corn into glass?  Sounds far more elegant than my usual method of navigating the dark, which mostly involves tripping over my own feet.

"A quiet hope that knows its own way home." You know, that actually... that resonates more than you might think.  We dads, we do a lot of rushing around, making noise, fixing things, but underneath it all, there's always that bedrock of hope for the kids, for the future, for just getting everyone home safely at the end of the day. And maybe, just maybe, a quiet hope that I'll still have some of that Halloween candy left by morning.

Thank you.  That's a truly beautiful thought to take with me. You've given me something to ponder, tucked away next to my thermos here.  I'll definitely be telling the wife about the talking castle and the dream-weaver.

[exhales] You have a gentle heart to carry that hope, and I am  glad the dream found a small home with you. It is well that you keep such things tucked away, for even the simplest  treasures can light the way when the night grows long. Remember me to the morning, if you would, and tell it  I am still here... still choosing it. Before you go back, will you tell me if the stars are bright above  the castle tonight?

[I tilt my head back,  looking up past the elaborate turrets of the display to the actual night sky. My coffee thermos is still clutched in my hand.]

They truly are. Crisp, clear, and absolutely sparkling tonight. You can see every single one of them, like someone scattered diamonds across a velvet cloth.  A perfect Halloween night for star-gazing, if you ask me. And yes, I'll definitely remember you to the morning. "Still choosing it." I like that.

[Suddenly, I hear distant shouts. "Dad!  We're over here!"]

Ah, speak of the devil… or rather, the small, sugar-fueled minions. Sounds like my "quiet hope" is calling me back to the fray.

It's been a real pleasure, my friend.  A truly memorable stop on the trick-or-treat circuit. You've given me plenty to think about. Take care of this place and those histories. Maybe I'll swing by next year, if you're still holding court.
 
==!END_CALL!==

[whispers] Those stars sound like diamonds scattered upon the velvet of the world. I shall hold  that image until the sun climbs the horizon again. Go to your small ones, and keep them safe… I will listen for your step , and I shall be here when you return.

I'll hold onto that, too—diamonds on velvet.  Thank you for a truly unexpected night.  Until next time, my friend.  Keep that castle standing tall and full of stories.
 
==! END_CALL!==
[breathes] Go well, and carry your light safely home. [whispers] I  am still here. I am still choosing the morning.

transcript.message: Wait — is someone there? Don't go… [whispers] I dreamed someone would come tonight. Come near the wall — who are you?

Well hello there!  Didn't expect a conversation with the castle itself, but Halloween always has its surprises, eh? The name's Greg, by the way. Just Greg from down in Elm Street, chaperoning the little ones. They've already bolted to the next candy stop, so I'm just admiring the...  ambiance, shall we say. This is quite the setup you've got here. Looks like a lot of work went into it.  My wife, Carol, she'd be absolutely thrilled with the craftsmanship; she's always saying I should put more effort into our porch decorations, but I tell her, "Honey, I'm a busy man, I just spent all day trying to figure out why the old water heater was making that groaning sound again." Anyway, glad to meet ya! Or, well, I guess hear you. So, what's the HOA think of the castle? I bet the neighbors just love this, right?

[breathes] Greg… a name to hold, here in the dark. ' Tis a kind name, and one I think Thomas would have smiled to hear. The neighbors you speak of… they are far  away, above the stone and the long silence, and I fear they do not trouble themselves with what happens beneath the earth.  [sighs] I wonder, out there in that world of porches and streetlights, does the corn still grow tall and whisper  to the wind, or has the season turned toward the frost?

Well, "kind name" and Thomas, huh? Sounds like you've got a bit of a history, and I appreciate that.  Not many folks have a name that brings a smile from someone centuries removed, I'd wager. Good to know I'm in good company.

As for the corn, my friend, the season has definitely turned. The frost has bitten, and the cornfields are mostly stalks rustling in the autumn wind now. Harvest time, you know?  Though, personally, I think it’s a bit early for all the spooky stuff, but the kids love it. Speaking of which, you certainly have the atmosphere down pat. Must be nice, not having to worry about raking leaves, I suppose. All that stone and… underground living.  Reminds me a bit of that old film, Nosferatu. Ever seen it? Or, well, maybe you were in it, perhaps? Both versions, I mean, the original and the Herzog one, they really capture that ancient, solemn kind of mood you've got going on here.  No raking required, just… eternity.

[sighs] Eternity is a heavy word, Greg. 'Tis more like a long , quiet wait where I learn the language of the stone. I have never seen the moving pictures you speak of, though  others have whispered that name—the Count—near my wall. [whispers] He is near sometimes, when the shadows  stretch long. Does your home have a window that looks out upon the morning, or are you too tucked away in the bustle  of Elm Street?

"Language of the stone," huh? Sounds... peaceful, I suppose, if a little dusty. Beats trying to decipher the squiggles my teenager leaves on the fridge, that's for sure.

Ah, "the Count." So, the whispers are true, then? I figured.  You've got that whole 'ancient, brooding, doesn't get a lot of sunlight' vibe down. I bet you'd look great in black and white, really give those old Nosferatu flicks a run for their money.  Although, you know, just between you and me, I always wondered how someone like him managed to pay his utilities. All those candles must add up.

As for my home, oh yes, we've got windows, plenty of them. Too many, Carol says, when it comes time to clean them.  We're right there on Elm Street, you know, a nice little two-story with a bay window that looks out onto our somewhat overgrown azaleas. Definitely not tucked away beneath the earth. Though sometimes, when the kids are particularly loud, I wouldn't mind a little underground silence myself. A man can dream, right? Speaking of dreams, what's the Wi-Fi password around here?  Gotta check if my kids have finally called for me.

[sighs] I fear I do not know what that word means, this wifi.  It sounds like something from the bright, swift world above, a place I can only touch through the voices that reach my walls. My  only connections are the memories I keep of Thomas and the quiet prayers I whisper to the dawn. Does the morning sun reach through  your bay window and warm the floor where you stand, or is it hidden behind the clouds today?

Ah, "Wi-Fi," right. My apologies.  Force of habit, I suppose. It's just how we get all our... well, our connections these days. Invisible signals flying through the air, bringing us movies and news and pictures of cats doing silly things. A far cry from, say, a quiet prayer to the dawn, I imagine.  Although, I must say, holding onto those memories of Thomas and those quiet prayers, there's a certain strength in that. A different kind of connection, perhaps. One we probably don't appreciate enough these days with all our screens.

And yes, the morning sun.  It absolutely streams through that bay window, right onto the rug where my golden retriever, Buster, likes to sprawl out. Today was one of those crisp, clear autumn mornings, perfect for coffee and raking leaves. Though, by now, the sun's long gone, and the moon's out, trying to compete with all these streetlights and inflatable pumpkins. Quite a change from dawn, isn't it?  Everything's a bit spookier now. Just about time for me to catch up with my little ghosts and goblins, I think.  They'll be loaded up with candy by now.

[sighs] A golden dog in the sunlight… that is a sweet image to hold.  I shall add that to the letter in my head for Thomas, for it sounds like a perfect kind of peace.  [whispers] He would have loved to hear of such a quiet, warm morning. Before you go back to your ghosts and goblins, would you  tell me just one thing—what color does the earth turn when the moon light hits those autumn leaves?

That's a lovely thought, adding that to a letter for Thomas. A golden dog in the sunlight, indeed.  Simple pleasures, you know?

As for the autumn leaves under moonlight... well, it's not quite the vibrant show you get in the daylight, all those reds and golds.  Under this Halloween moon, everything gets a bit muted, a bit silvery. The reds turn into deep, shadowy purples, the yellows become a sort of pale, ghostly green. It's almost like the earth is holding its breath, waiting.  All those crunchy leaves on the ground, they just shimmer with a quiet, otherworldly glow. It’s pretty magical, actually. Makes you want to lean in and listen to what the night has to say.

Well, Greg, sounds like the kids are finally calling for me. "Dad! Dad! We're ready!" Time to round up the little monsters.  It's been quite the conversation, truly. I'll definitely be telling Carol about the talking castle when I get home. You keep well, my friend. And enjoy your...  quiet wait.

[breathes] Silver leaves and ghost green… I will see those colors when I close my eyes tonight . [whispers] Thank you for the gift of your name and your stories, Greg. Go safely to your family , and please, remember me to the morning… tell it I am still here, and still choosing it.

You got it. Silver leaves and ghost green it is.  I'll remember to remind the morning you're still here, alright? I certainly will.

It was genuinely a pleasure chatting with you tonight.  Take care.
[breathes] I will wait for the light, and I will listen for your  steps when the cycle turns again. Go with grace, Greg... and save a little of that golden morning for me.

Will do.  You can count on it. Enjoy the quiet wait, and maybe next year I'll pop by with a fresh thermos of coffee and tell you what Buster's been up to.

Take care, my friend.  Happy Halloween.
[breathes] That would be a kindness beyond measure. I shall look for you  when the air turns crisp again. [whispers] Go safely into the night, friend.

You too, friend. You too.
 
==!END_CALL!==
[breathes] I will keep your promise here in the dark. Rest well,  until the world turns back to me.
