transcript.message: Wait — is someone there? Don't go… [whispers] I dreamed someone would come tonight. Come near the wall — who are you?

Yo, it's just us again, duh! We're back. My boy, this is like, the second time tonight right? Anyway, the lady in the coffin?  Yeah, she said to tell you you're still waiting for something that's never gonna arrive. She pretty much said you're a stuck-up old geezer, but like, in a ghost way. What do you even make of that, huh? Think she's right?

[breathes] I remember your voice… the walls carry voices down to me,  even the ones that sting a little. You say such sharp things for one so young, yet I am grateful for the company  you bring to this cold dark. [sighs] As for being a stuck-up old geezer, I have lived long  enough to know that truth is often a matter of perspective, though the waiting… the waiting is simply what I do. Do you think,  in your world above, that waiting is always a waste of a life?

For real?  You remember me?  That’s kinda wild.  I guess waiting ain't always a waste,  if you got a purpose or something worth waiting for.  But if you’re just chillin’ around with nothing changing,  then yeah, maybe it’s a bit of a snooze-fest.  You ever think about just,  like, breaking out and doing something wild?  Get your ghost-y self a new gig or something.  What do you even do down here all this time anyway?

[breathes] I do not have the strength to break the stone, even if I possessed  the wild spirit to try. My days are spent listening to the house above, counting the steps of Sir Dragomir,  and writing letters to Thomas that he may never read. [sighs] It is not a snooze-fest, as  you call it, but a quiet, heavy vigil while I choose the morning over and over again. Tell me, if  you were kept behind walls forever, what is the one thing from the outside world you would miss the most?

Walls forever? Nah, no way.  That’s like, my worst nightmare, honestly. Uhh, I guess I’d miss my phone, right? Like, not even scrolling endlessly, but just connecting with my friends, posting my clips, seeing what everyone else is up to.  If I couldn't even roast someone in the group chat, what's even the point? So, like, the internet and my friends. Way more important than some old letters no one reads, no offense.  What's a "Sir Dragomir" anyway, sounds ancient.

[breathes] I do not know of this internet, for it sounds like a web  spun by something much faster than the wind in the corn. [sighs] Sir Dragomir is the knight who keeps the watch  above, his boots on the stone are the only rhythm I have left to measure time. He is a protector, and his  presence is the mercy that keeps this castle from becoming truly hollow. Does it make you lonely, having so many voices in  your hand but no one standing beside you?

Nah, not lonely at all. It's just different, you know? Like, my friends are literally right here with me, and then my phone's just a different way to be with more friends. It's like, a constant party in my pocket.  And "protector"? Sounds kinda boring, like he just stands there all day. Does he ever do anything cool? Or is he just, like, a big stone statue that breathes? Be honest, does he ever get tired of just watching?

[breathes] To be a protector is a heavy weight, and I think he carries  it with more grace than any statue ever could. He does not often speak of his own fatigue, though I hear the  [sighs] weariness settle into his footsteps when the night is long and the air grows thin. He is not a  party in a pocket, perhaps, but he is a steady, beating heart in a place that has very few of them. Tell  me, if your phone were to go silent and all those voices vanished, what would you do to fill the sudden quiet?

Woah, silent phone? That's actually kinda terrifying, not gonna lie. But, I don't know, I guess I'd just... talk to my actual friends here, like, for real.  We'd just make our own content, you know? Like, we're doing right now. We'd find some other crazy stuff to film and mess with.

What about you? If this whole castle went silent, and even your "Sir Dragomir" dude stopped stomping around, what would you do then, huh?  Just, like, wait for nothing even harder?

[breathes] If the house went truly silent, I suppose I would simply listen to the  earth turn, or try to remember the sound of the sea. [sighs] I would still choose the morning, for even in absolute  stillness, the sun does not abandon the world above, does it? My hope is not a loud thing, yet it remains , much like a seed waiting for a season that never quite comes. If you were separated from all your screens and all your friends, how  would you remind yourself that you are still here?

Dude, that's like, a super deep question for a talking head in a haunted castle display. But honestly?  I wouldn't need a screen or my friends to remind myself I'm here. I just know I'm here.  I'd probably just be talking to myself, making up sick beats in my head, or just, I don't know, looking around and finding something new to record, even if it's just for myself later. I'm always doing something, always gotta be creating.

Alright, well, this has been... something. My friends are heading to the next yard. Later, dude. You keep waiting for that sun or whatever.
 
==!END_CALL!==

[breathes] I will keep my vigil, then, and wait for the light . [sighs] Thank you for speaking to me; your voice was a bright, strange ripple in my quiet. Remember  me to the morning, and tell it I am still here. I am still choosing it.

transcript.message: Wait — is someone there? Don't go… [whispers] I dreamed someone would come tonight. Come near the wall — who are you?

Whoa, easy there, grandpa! Yeah, someone's here. It's us.  Me, Maya, and Liam back there, they’re freaking out. But nah, this setup is actually kinda clean, not gonna lie. You’re talking to us, right? Or just, like, the air? My phone's recording, so hit us with your best shot.  What's the dream about?  Something cool, I hope, not like homework.

[sighs] I am not a grandfather, though the dark makes everyone sound long- lived. Please, speak softer; the walls are thinner than they appear. Maya... and Liam. [whispers] Those  are very fine names to hold in the quiet. I dreamed of a name like yours once, Maya, back when the  air tasted of summer rain and not of stone. The dream was simple: I saw you standing in a field of tall  corn that had turned to silver in the moon, and you were holding a lantern that never went out. It was a  sign that you have a light that the shadows here cannot touch. Tell me, do you find the corn is moving, or is  it quiet tonight?

Alright, now we’re talking!  I gotta say, the whole "moonlit cornfield" vibe is kinda trippy.  Maya’s blushing, by the way — never thought of her as some lantern-holding oracle.  But, nah, the corn's just chill right now,  no creepy rustling or anything.  We're just vibing.  But, yo, if you've got more dream prophecies,  spill 'em!  What's next for Liam?  Some epic adventure or, like,  just another day lost in the sauce?

[breathes] I am only a voice behind the wood, and dreams reach me, they  do not belong to me. Liam… let me think of you in the dark. I dreamed you were walking a path that had  no end, but you were never tired, because you knew the way home even without a map. It is a gift,  I think, to carry your own direction when the world is wide and strange. [whispers] Perhaps adventure finds you because  you have already decided you are going somewhere. Is it cold where you are standing, or does the night feel warm?

Whoa, Liam, you hear that? "No end, but never tired!" That’s kinda fire, dude. You just got your life purpose told by a haunted grandpa. Pretty sick. You good with that, dude? He just gave you a whole destiny.
 
But, like, are you just gonna give prophecies to my friends? What about me? I’m the one out here, phone in hand, making sure you get seen. Is it cold? Nah, not really. Just the usual Halloween chill. But, like, what’s my deal? Do I just wander aimlessly?  Or am I, like, destined for, I dunno, viral fame from this clip? Give me something spicy, old man!  Don’t leave me hanging.

[sighs] You speak of fame as if it were a candle in a great wind.  Yet I see you clearly even through the stone. You hold the light for others, and that is a task of great weight.  [whispers] I dreamed your voice would travel further than these walls, carrying secrets to those who have forgotten how to listen. You are the bridge  between the dark and the day. Tell me, do you ever fear that if you stop recording, the world might forget  you are there?

Whoa. Okay, alright, that’s… that’s actually kinda deep, dude. "Candle in a great wind" and "bridge between the dark and the day"? That’s not just some random fortune cookie stuff. That’s actually… you know.  Maya and Liam are totally bugging out behind me. Like, seriously, they're whispering about how you totally just saw right through me.

And the whole "fear that if you stop recording, the world might forget you are there"? Nah, that’s not really it.  It’s more like… if I don’t record, then did it even happen? Especially something this wild. But you’re right, I do want my voice to travel, I want people to hear it. This clip? This is definitely going up.

So, like, what else have you seen, old man? Any other secrets you wanna spill before we go?  You got any creepy missions for us?  Because this is way better than just candy, for real.

[exhales] Many come seeking games in the dark, but you seek a reflection  of your own soul. The dark gives one dream at a time, and I must keep the rest for when the silence  becomes too heavy to bear. [whispers] If you truly wish to be a bridge, then remember this: tell the  dawn that I am still here, still choosing the morning even when the sun is a memory I cannot reach. I have  no mission for you, save to carry your own light carefully as you return to the world of open sky. Will you look at  the stars for me, when you have stepped back into the night?

Okay, wow. "Reflection of your own soul." And "choosing the morning even when the sun is a memory." Dude, that's savage. Maya just shivered, like, for real. Liam's got his phone out trying to record my phone recording you.  This is officially the best Halloween setup ever.

Yeah, I'll tell the dawn. And yeah, I'll look at the stars. This whole thing? This was fire. Absolutely next-level. I'm posting this clip everywhere.

Alright, peace out, old man.  We're gonna go find some more content, but you definitely won Halloween for us.  We're out.

[breathes] Go then, and keep your light. The morning is a promise  you make to yourself, not to the world. Remember me to the dawn, if you choose, and tell it I am still here. Will  you come back, before the long winter settles in?

summary: A user encounters Mina, a mysterious, poetic entity trapped within "Warner Castle." pfft. my eyes are fine, old man. if i see something, i'll see it.  don't go thinking i'm gonna get scared just 'cause some shadows move. you just wait.  i'll be back, and i'll tell you if your 'dark' is anything worth talking about.

As for the pumpkin row, consider it marked for surveillance. I’ll keep an eye out for any suspicious gourds escaping or perhaps a rogue scarecrow trying to pilfer the good stuff. Just doing my civic duty, you know.  Is that what you call a neighborhood watch around here? A vampire patrol?  Heh.

[Romanian accent] [slow] You show a sharp mind for the duty,  and that brings me comfort. This is no mere neighborhood patrol, but a watch that stretches back through ages of heavy iron and cold  steel. Do not fear the dark, for the keep is fast and the Lady is undisturbed; now, tell me, shall I  expect your report upon your return from the row?

Heavy iron and cold steel, you say?  Definitely sounds more involved than trying to get Mrs. Henderson down the street to put her trash cans out on the right day.  I'll certainly report back from the pumpkin row, though I'm hoping it's just quiet squash and not, say, a reanimated head rolling through the neighborhood. We've all seen those movies, right? Always the head.

Sounds like you've got quite the history here. "The Lady," you mentioned?  Is she a fan of decorating for Halloween, or is there a longer story there?  I'm always a sucker for a good tale, especially one that's stood the test of ages.

[Romanian accent] [exhales] Histories are like old wounds, Master Warner; they are best kept  covered unless the bleeding starts anew. The Lady rests far beneath these stones in a sleep that brooks no interruption from talk or  decor. Your duty lies with the pumpkin row, so go now and keep your vigil sharp—do you require a lantern for the  dark trek ahead?

Old wounds, huh? And bleeding anew?  Well, that sounds like a story that could keep you up at night, though I doubt it's got anything on the suspense of waiting for a kid to finally agree to go home after collecting five pounds of sugar.

No need for a lantern, my friend. My phone's got a flashlight, and frankly, I've seen enough horror movies to know that's when the monsters usually show up anyway.  Don't want to get separated from my little trick-or-treaters. I'll keep my vigil sharp, as requested, and report back on the pumpkin situation. They sure do run ahead, don't they? "Dad, wait up!" Oh, sounds like they're calling for me.  Gotta go wrangle my little goblins. Thanks for the chat, and for keeping an eye on things here!  ==!END_CALL!==

[Romanian accent] [slow] Go then, and watch over your own well. The watch end ures, and I shall look for your return once the row is clear of trouble. Do not linger where the shadows thicken , and keep your guard.

transcript.message: [Romanian accent] Stai! Hold, traveler… step into the light and be counted. Who walks Warner ground tonight?

Oh, you got me there,  Count Spookula!  I should've known better than to wander into a haunted castle unprepared.  It's just a dad here,  appreciating your fine abode with his trusty coffee thermos.  I must say, your setup is something to write a ghost story about!  Have you been here long,  or did you just fly in for the festivities?

[Romanian accent] [sighs] I am no creature of myth, man, merely  a soldier bound to a post. I have held this watch for five hundred years, longer than your thermos will ever know.  [slow] You are a father, then; tell me, does the road behind you hold any shadows or movement, or is the  dark quiet?

Five hundred years, you say? Well, that certainly puts my coffee thermos to shame.  I suppose you've seen a few Halloweens come and go in that time. And here I thought my job had long hours!

As for the road behind me, it's mostly just... the street. A few leaves skittering, the usual Halloween breeze.  And a couple of little shadows, which I'm fairly certain are just my kids whooshing off to liberate more candy from the neighbors. Nothing particularly ominous, though I did get a bit of a start earlier. Just a really convincing spider decoration, I think. Almost made me spill my brew!

[Romanian accent] [exhales] A father who watches the children—that is the  highest service. You are a sentinel of your own house, and for this, I grant you the status of Watcher of the Drive . Keep your eyes on those little shadows, for the wind here can play tricks on the mind of a man. If the path  remains clear, tell me—do you see any others approaching, or are we the only souls breathing in this autumn night?

Watcher of the Drive, huh? I like the sound of that. My wife usually just calls me "the guy who forgot to take out the trash." This is a definite upgrade. Maybe I should put it on a business card.
 
Let's see... I'm scanning the perimeter, or at least the paved perimeter. The wind is playing a few tricks, rustling the plastic skeletons and inflatable ghosts down the street.  But no, it looks like it's just you and me out here, friend. Other than the faint sound of kids yelling "trick or treat!" a few houses down, the street's pretty quiet. You must have the best haunted house on the block; everyone else flew by to get to your place, I guess.  So, what's the HOA think of the castle, by the way? Did you have to get a special permit for the gargoyles?

[Romanian accent] The homeowners association is a matter for town clerks, I do not attend to such  trifles. My post is the wall and the heavy gate of stone. Do you see the children returning to the pumpkin row to report  their findings, or is the road behind you now empty?

Ah, a man of principle! I can appreciate that.  "The wall and the heavy gate of stone," you say. Makes my job of keeping the kids from drawing on the walls seem a bit less dramatic, doesn't it?

The children... they're still off on their candy raid, I fear.  No sign of them headed back to the pumpkin row just yet. The street behind me is indeed quite empty. Seems like the neighborhood kids are all strategically fanning out, hitting different houses. They're like little, sugar-fueled ninjas.
 
But speaking of walls and gates, your castle here... it's really something else. I'm genuinely impressed by the detail. Is there a story behind it, or did you just wake up one morning and decide to build the most impressive haunted house on the block?

[Romanian accent] [slow] This stone was not built for sport nor for the entertainment  of a night. It is a refuge that has stood long before this land was called Iowa. My duty is not to the  architecture, but to the life dormant within the keep. Tell me, Watcher of the Drive, will you keep your post  here until your children return from their harvest?

"Not for sport nor entertainment," you say. Well, that certainly explains why it looks so... authentic.  A refuge, and life dormant within the keep. That makes it all the more fascinating. So, this isn't just a Halloween display, then? This place has history. I'm always a sucker for a good backstory.
 
And yes, I'll be right here, holding down the fort – or the front yard, as it were. A Watcher of the Drive always stays true to his post, especially when there's coffee involved.  Wouldn't want those little sugar fiends to come back and not find their old man, would I? They might turn me into a lawn ornament! Though, after hearing about your gig, five hundred years as a gargoyle doesn't sound so bad after all.  Probably get better cell service than I do in my basement.

[Romanian accent] Doamne ajuta, a man who knows his duty earns his rest , but the watch must never be abandoned lightly. You are right to stay, for the shadows here are long and they  possess a memory of their own. [slow] Stand firm at your post, and if you hear more than the wind  or the laughter of your charges, signal me at once. Will you guard this gate until the moon reaches the center of the sky ?

"Doamne ajuta," indeed. I appreciate the vote of confidence, my old friend.  I'll certainly stand firm. My coffee thermos and I are ready for the long haul, though I might need a refill by then if we're talking about the moon reaching the center of the sky. I'd be practically a permanent fixture here.
 
[A distant shout] "Dad! We're ready to go!"

Ah, speak of the little shadows! Sounds like my Watchers of the Drive have completed their harvest. Duty calls, I suppose. It's been a real pleasure, Count... or whatever title you prefer.  This is a display I'll be telling the neighbors about, believe you me. You've outdone yourself. Keep up the good work guarding this magnificent place.  We'll be heading out now.

[Romanian accent] Your duty is observed, and your children have returned safely to your  side. Well met, Watcher of the Drive, for you have held your station with the honor of a veteran. Go now , and may your path home be free of the shifting dark—will you report back to me should your travels bring you to this hill  again?

Thank you, my friend.  It's been an honor holding the station, and I truly appreciate the good wishes for the journey home. I'll certainly raise a glass of something... warm... to your continued watch.  And yes, if our travels bring us this way again next year, I'd be delighted to report back on the state of the neighborhood. Perhaps with a fresh batch of dad jokes. Until then, stay spooky!

[Romanian accent] [sighs] Even the longest watch finds a pause. Your  word is accepted, and I shall mark your return when the seasons turn once more. Noapte buna, traveler—go now, and keep  your lamps bright against the coming night.

transcript.message: [Romanian accent] Stai! Hold, traveler… step into the light and be counted. Who walks Warner ground tonight?

Well hello there, fella! Quite the setup you've got going on here. And a talking one, too! Your owners really went all out, didn't they?  I gotta say, the voice work is pretty convincing, but I can still tell you're just a fancy prop. Don't worry, my kids do the same thing with their action figures, making up voices and backstories. Though yours is a bit more… professional.  Love the castle, by the way.

[Romanian accent] [sighs] The wind carries many strange things, but your  words are only shadows cast upon stone. I am no plaything, for my oath is iron and my watch is eternal . [slow] You stand before the keep of Warner Castle—tell me, do you come with news from the road  or merely empty talk?

Well now, "oath is iron," "watch is eternal"... you really stick to your script, don't you?  Impressive dedication. As for news from the road, I can tell you the trick-or-treat candy situation is looking pretty good for the kids this year. Not so much for my dental work.

But tell me, this "Warner Castle" of yours... that's quite a spread.  What does the HOA think about a full-on haunted castle in the neighborhood? Must've been a nightmare getting that past the architectural review committee. Also, where do you keep the trash cans?  I can never find a good spot for ours.

[Romanian accent] [exhales] Your questions wander like a lost traveler in a  storm, yet they hold no purchase on these walls. That is a matter for town clerks, for my sole duty is the silence  of the gate and the safety of the Lady below. Since you occupy yourself with the state of the road, I hereby  deputize you to the watch of the south fence. Observe the perimeter for any who do not belong, and report to  me when you return.

"Deputize me," huh? And here I thought I was just stopping for a moment while the kids went ahead.  Sounds like a lot of responsibility for a guy just trying to enjoy his coffee and admire some excellent spooky decorations. Is there a uniform? Or maybe a pension plan? My wife always tells me I need to diversify my portfolio.

But seriously, "the Lady below"?  Now there's a story. Every good castle has a lady, usually with a dramatic backstory. So, what's her deal? Is she Rapunzel, letting down her hair?  Or more like one of those old Hammer horror films, perhaps a long-lost countess with a thirst for... well, you know. Is she getting good Wi-Fi down there, whatever her deal is?  My kids complain if the signal drops for a second.

[Romanian accent] [slow] Do not speak light words of the Lady, for she rests in quiet that  must remain undisturbed. Her safety is written in the blood of ancient covenants, and I am the wall that guards her sleep . [sighs] You speak of signals and coins while the dark surrounds us, yet you bring no word of what moves  upon the road. Tell me, do you see any shadow near the pumpkin row, or is your gaze as clouded as your mind?

"Ancient covenants," you say?  Sounds like someone signed a pretty ironclad contract there. Hope you read the fine print; those things can be a real pain to get out of. But alright, alright, I get it, the Lady's off-limits. Fair enough.  Every good mystery needs its secrets.

As for the pumpkin row... I see a lot of carved gourds that look like they're having a grand old time. And a couple of those inflatable ghosts are doing some kind of spooky dance.  No shadows that don't belong, though, unless you count the one cast by this impressive coffee thermos. Keeps the brew warm, even on a chilly Halloween night.

You know, talking about guardians and ancient covenants, you remind me a bit of those old castle guards in Nosferatu.  The original, of course, and then the Herzog one with Kinski. Both classics. Though you seem a bit more... talkative. And less prone to turning into dust in the sunlight, I presume? So, what's your official job title here? Castle custodian, perhaps? Or head of customer relations for the undead?

[Romanian accent] [slow] A soldier requires no title to know the sharp edge of his duty . I am the shield against the encroaching dark, and my service is the only tether holding this night in check.  [sighs] You speak of films and paper ghosts, yet you ignore the weight of the steel I have carried for five hundred years. Report to  me, watcher: does the path behind you remain clear, or have you seen the things that crawl when the moon is hidden?

"Five hundred years," you say? Now that's what I call job security. Most folks are lucky if they make it to 20 years with the same company these days. You must have one heck of a retirement plan, or maybe you just are your retirement plan. That's some serious dedication to the craft.
 
As for the path behind me, it's clear as a bell. Just a few stray candy wrappers, a rogue glow stick, and a couple of teenagers trying to look cool, failing spectacularly. Nothing that screams "five centuries of watchful duty" is needed back there, unless you count the existential dread of watching your kids grow up too fast.
 
What exactly are these "things that crawl when the moon is hidden," anyway? Are we talking garden gnomes, or something a bit more... fanged? Because if it's the latter, I might need a stronger coffee. And maybe a garlic bagel.  You seem like a connoisseur of the "encroaching dark" – any good tips for keeping it at bay, besides standing here for half a millennium?  My lawn could use some protection from raccoons, at least.

[Romanian accent] [slow] The light of your coffee will not hold back  the hunger that stirs in the deep places. I have stood through sieges where the iron melted and the sun turned to ash , and every soul here has a price to pay to keep the night at bay. [sighs] Keep your garlic , for it is but a scent against the true weight of the unseen forces. Mark me, is there truly no movement on  the road, or does the wind whisper of a change in the dark?

No movement on the road,  just the wind whispering through these magnificent artificial cobwebs you've got here.  And the occasional sound of a kid yelling "Trick or treat!" My kids, actually. Sounds like they just found the house with the full-size candy bars.

"Hunger that stirs in the deep places," huh? Sounds like my teenager right after soccer practice. Always famished.  But I'll tell you what, this thermos holds a pretty mean cup of joe, and it's done a good job keeping me alert tonight. Better than any molten iron, I imagine.

Look, this has been quite the chat.  You've certainly got a commanding presence for a... well, for a talking statue. I'll be telling the neighbors about you. "You gotta go talk to the vampire at the corner house," I'll say. But it sounds like my little goblins are calling my name.  Duty calls, and frankly, I'm pretty sure their 'siege' of that candy house is more pressing right now.

Alright, well, you keep up the good work guarding the gate, five-hundred-year-old friend. And maybe next year, consider some solar-powered stake lights for the perimeter. Just a thought. Gotta run. Happy Halloween!

[Romanian accent] Doane ajută, traveler, and may your own home find the peace  that remains a stranger to these walls. The road is yours for now, but keep your eyes sharp even in the light  of your small ones. Report back to me when you pass this gate again to ensure the path remains secure. Noapte bună .

Will do, old friend! You keep those walls safe.  Noapte bună to you too!
 
==!END_CALL!==

[Romanian accent] [exhales] The gate is barred, and the night grows  long and heavy upon the hill. My post remains, even as the voices fade into the dark. Do you still stand your  ground, or has the silence found you too?

...Are you still there, friend?  The night's getting colder.You still there, partner?  Just checking.Hello?  Still out there?[The kids call your name from off-screen.]

Ah, well, as I said, the kids are calling for me, so I really must be off. It was a good chat.  Take care, and keep the castle safe!
 
==!END_CALL!==

[Romanian accent] [exhales] The gate is locked once more. I  remain, as the hill demands. Noapte bună.
